mechanisms: BUF_MEM adoption of the decoded data
DER read loop BUF_MEM_grow and BIO_read
file_dispositions.note: The authority declares `unsigned int length` and stores strtol's result there; the port kept a c_long, so `-length -1` remained negative instead of becoming 4294967295 and being clamped to `num`. `length` is now c_uint with `(unsigned int)num` clamping and an `(int)length` write comparison. The read loop's checked_add growth, the OB-1 adoption of `name`/`header`, the BUF_MEM data ownership and all three release paths are sound; PEM failure blocks are already freed and nulled by PEM_read_bio_ex.

mechanisms: cipher stack bounds and description buffer
file_dispositions.note: The supported-cipher stack is freed once and only under `use_supported`, `ctx`/`ssl` are freed on every path, and the stdout/stderr BIOs are BIO_NOCLOSE. `OPENSSL_sk_num(NULL)` answers -1, so a failed supported-cipher stack yields an empty loop rather than an out-of-bounds access. dummy_psk holds no state and cannot re-enter.

The detached-content BIO written through `indata` was never released; the authority frees it with BIO_free(indata) at apps/cms.c:1512. It is now owned by DetachedBio, whose Drop releases it on every exit. CMS_add1_signer up-refs signer and key (crypto/cms/cms_sd.c:369-378), so the post-call releases are correct rather than double frees.

The NCONF_get_section_names stack was never released; the authority calls sk_OPENSSL_CSTRING_free(sections) at apps/configutl.c:201. It is now released with OPENSSL_sk_free on both exits after the call. The stack was created without an element freefunc and its names are owned by cnf, so stack-only release is the authority's semantics. The default-config OwnedBlock and the CONF_VALUE borrows are sound.

Field prints were sent to the -out BIO, but the authority prints them to bio_out before opening out at apps/crl.c:387-389. The -hash <ERROR> arm also broke the loop and continued to write the CRL, where the authority executes `goto end`. Prints now use a BIO_NOCLOSE stdout BIO opened first; out is opened after the print loop; every exit releases print_out, out and x exactly once.

Every early exit between the BIO allocations and the final release leaked the owned BIOs, digest, key and context. A single dgst_cleanup now performs the authority's exact order: BIO_free(in), BIO_free_all(out), EVP_MD_free(md), EVP_PKEY_free(sigkey), EVP_MD_CTX_free(signctx), BIO_free(bmd). Freeing inb before bmd matches apps/dgst.c:506-512; BIO_free does not traverse the filter chain. EVP_MD_free is a no-op for the legacy/static methods the digest parser may return.

strtol_base0 accumulated into i128 with unchecked multiply/add, so a long numeric argument could panic in debug or wrap in release before the range check. It now uses saturating_mul/saturating_add, matching asn1parse; overflow still becomes an out-of-range answer. All pkey/out/ctx exits release once.

All pkey/out/ectx/pub_key exits release once and the encoder NULL/number-of-encoders path is safe. Retained shared divergence: the authority's bio_open_owner() owner-only permissions are not reconstructed, so a private-key -out uses bio_open_default/fopen semantics; `private` is computed but unused. This is the existing apps/lib boundary recorded by keyio, not a new assumption.

defects.description: NCONF_get_section_names returns a newly allocated stack; neither normal nor -out-failure exit released it.
defects.repair: OPENSSL_sk_free(sections) on both exits after the call.

defects.description: The detached-content BIO set through SMIME_read_CMS_ex's bcont was used by CMS_verify and never released; the authority frees indata at apps/cms.c:1512.
defects.repair: DetachedBio RAII owner with BIO_free in Drop.

defects.description: Early returns after the BIO/digest/key allocations skipped the authority's end: release list.
defects.repair: dgst_cleanup helper called on every exit, preserving the authority's release order.

defects.description: strtol_base0 multiplied and added into i128 without saturation; an over-long numeric option can panic in debug or wrap in release.
defects.repair: saturating_mul/saturating_add before the existing range check.

defects.description: Selected fields were printed to the -out BIO instead of bio_out, and the -hash <ERROR> arm continued into text/writer output instead of bailing at end:.
defects.repair: A BIO_NOCLOSE stdout print BIO is opened first; out is opened after the print loop; the hash failure returns after releasing print_out/x.

defects.description: length was c_long while the authority stores strtol in unsigned int, so a negative -length was not converted and clamped as the authority does.
defects.repair: length is c_uint, clamped with (unsigned int)num and compared to BIO_write as (int)length.

retained_obligations: src/apps/dsa.rs (with src/apps/keyio.rs): the authority's bio_open_owner() owner-only permissions are not reconstructed; a private-key -out uses bio_open_default/fopen semantics. Shared apps/lib boundary, not new to this batch.
src/apps/cms.rs and src/apps/dsa.rs: the pointer-bearing ERR_print_errors tails are not reproduced on load/final failures; the behavioral message is printed.

src/apps/crl.rs: repeated print options (for example -issuer -issuer) print once per occurrence, while the authority's per-option index prints the option once at its last position. No court drives duplicates.

src/apps/configutl.rs: -out is written at the end rather than opened before the config load; only unopenable -out side effects differ.
